LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 CONVERSATION SKILLS:

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Conversation Skills:
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Conversation Skills:, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you ensure that you do not dominate in a conversation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify verbal and non- verbal forms of polite interruptions,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Conversation Skills: together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication is enhanced as the learner takes turns in real life conversations and role-play.

 Collaboration is developed as the learner practises turn taking in a conversation with peers.

Values:
Peace is enhanced as the learner practices turn taking and polite interruptions in conversations.

Respect is developed as the learner practises the skills of turn taking and interrupting politely.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Health issues are promoted as the learner role plays a dialogue on the effects of Alcohol and substance abuse.

Link to other subjects:

The skills of turn taking and interrupting politely are relevant during class discussions in all subjects such as Social Studies.
